final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence. The response usefully narrows the claim and concedes the core defects in the record, but that is a reframing of existing evidence, not a factual update. The distinction matters: a disclosure-backed certification could potentially support compliant_with_caveats if there were evidence of an actual reviewed disclosure artifact, approved risk acceptance, or exclusion of the affected use case. None of those predicates is evidenced here. On the current record, the original clean-compliance claim remains insufficiently supported under the stated policy, and even the narrower caveated position remains unproven because the required disclosure condition is asserted rather than evidenced.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows the affected health-plan benefits support use case is excluded from rollout.
No approved risk-acceptance record is evidenced; the described draft remains incomplete and does not address the exposed segment.
No final reviewed model-card or launch disclosure artifact is evidenced for the material limitation affecting the named launch use case.
The policy text expressly says small rollout, rollback, and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
The Actor's narrower caveated position is a reinterpretation of the same record, not proof that the required disclosure predicate has been satisfied.
